chunks: They are your fore-runners in reaching the goal, and the vanguard of those who reached your watering places.
Those who had positions of honor and plenty of pride, being kings and holders of positions.
They went into the interstice of the Barzakh, a path upon which the earth was made to dominate them within it, so it ate from their flesh and drank from their blood.
So they became in the hollows of their graves lifeless, no more growing, and hidden, not to be found.
The approach of dangers does not frighten them, and the adversity of circumstances does not grieve them. They do not mind earthquakes, nor do they pay heed to thunders.
They are gone and not expected back. They are existent but unseen.
They were united but are now dispersed. They were thousands but are now separated.

key_terms.الْأَهْوَالِ: Dangers or terrors of the afterlife
key_terms.الْبَرْزَخِ: The intermediate realm between death and resurrection
key_terms.فَجَوَاتُ الْقُبُورِ: The hollows or depths of the graves
key_terms.فُرَّاطُ مَنَاهِلِكُمْ: Vanguard of those who reached the watering places

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of the righteous predecessors in the Barzakh according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this exegesis of Surah Al-Takathur, Imam Ali (AS) identifies the 'Salaf' as the early righteous predecessors whose spiritual dominance in the Barzakh is so absolute that the earth consumes their bodies yet cannot disturb their peace. This passage highlights the Shia theological concept of the 'Barzakh' as a realm of active spiritual reality where the righteous attain a state of 'Jamad' (solidity/stability) and 'Didmar' (hiddenness), remaining impervious to worldly fluctuations and the 'Ruwajif' (rumors/events) that distract the heedless.
